newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Greek singer says Ariane will finally take off.
newsitem.headline: Greek singer says Ariane will finally take off.

text.p: Greek singer Nana Mouskouri predicted on Wednesday that a European Union programme to help translate and distribute books written in lesser-known EU languages would finally be adopted.

"I do not think the British will block the programme. They are on our side now," Mouskouri, who became a Euro-MP in 1994, told Reuters after the European Parliament's culture committee unanimously backed her report on the scheme.
"Maybe they didn't realise it is really not one way. Books in English can be translated into minority languages too," Mouskouri said.

Last year Britain single-handedly blocked the 34-million-Ecu Ariane programme, which would provide EU money to promote the translation of books and plays from and into languages like Welsh, Basque and Gaelic.
Britain said at the time that the scheme concentrated too much on translating and would be a waste of money.
Later, in a compromise designed to push the programme through, the Culture Council agreed to cut the programme from five to two years and axe its planned budget fivefold, to seven million Ecus.
Mouskouri said she expected the parliament to endorse the draft decision, COM(94)356, on October 22. It needs the approval of Euro-MPs and the unanimous support of ministers to become law.
But she said she would urge the parliament to accept no less than 10.5 million Ecus, which means the bargaining with Britain is not totally over.
"Ariane is not so expensive but it is very important. It is about communicating knowledge," she said.

Mouskouri, who sings in six European languages, said she personally preferred to read books in the original if possible but thought it was important to have good translations which respected "the spirit, feeling and identity of the writer".
"There are no politics in this. How can we fight about culture?" she said.
